solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Introductory cruise arranged during Test avoiding roundabout?

indicators.note: during says the rearranged cruise comes in the middle of the trimmed test word
avoiding says the test word goes without the roundabout letter

parts.note: to test something is to prove it, as in proving a theory
a roundabout is circular, so it stands for the round letter O

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of cruise are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday cruise is booked in the middle of a Test match series, while the traveller dodges traffic islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' looks like cricket but is the verb, as in proving a theory; 'avoiding' and 'arranged' work on separate pieces, with the scrambled cruise placed 'during' the shortened test word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precursive comes before and leads into what follows, so it serves as an introduction or forerunner.

clue.text: One principally getting much intercourse?

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of the word getting
much, rather than all, says the word for intercourse loses its last letter

parts.note: getting one's oats is slang for having sex, so oats stands for intercourse

explanation.surface: A wry question about someone who has a busy love life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' trims OATS to OAT. Read whole, the clue describes a randy male, which is the slang sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A goat, especially an old goat, is slang for a lecherous man who chases sex.

clue.text: Actress's tree-lined ground introduced by relative with wealth

parts.note: a mother, or ma, is a close relative

indicators.note: ground, as in ground down or crushed, says the letters of tree-lined are broken up and re-formed

parts.note: having wealth means being rich

explanation.surface: An actress owns a tree-lined estate, inherited from a wealthy relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like land or an estate, but it is the past tense of grind and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-born film star of the 1930s and 1940s, famous for The Blue Angel.

clue.text: Country's level of intelligence restricts soldiers

indicators.note: restricts says the intelligence measure hems in the soldiers, holding them inside

parts.note: IQ, the intelligence quotient, measures a level of intelligence
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of British soldiers

explanation.surface: A nation's intelligence services are said to keep its army in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Country's' stands for 'has', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a nation in the Middle East, with Baghdad as its capital.

clue.text: If there's civilisation, hostile forces arise

parts.note: the Incas were the great pre-Columbian civilisation of Peru

indicators.note: arise in a down clue says the enemy word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy, a hostile force

explanation.surface: A warning that where civilisation flourishes, enemies will spring up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arise' works upward because this is a down clue; 'there's' is only a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as a conditional connective, so 'in the event that' can replace 'if'.

clue.text: Fabric centres in Anjou? Bear north

indicators.note: centres in points to the middle letters of each of the two named words

explanation.surface: A question about the textiles made in central Anjou, with a nudge northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of Anjou is J and the middle of Bear is EA; N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is a strong twilled cotton cloth, the material that blue denim trousers were once made from.

clue.text: Study love letter in moving train, and feel thrilled

indicators.note: in says the study word and the letter go inside the rearranged train
moving says the letters of train shift into a new order

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
love is zero in tennis, and the letter shaped like zero is O

explanation.surface: Someone reads a love letter on a moving train and is overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' scrambles train so that its T stands apart at the front, letting the study word and love letter slip 'in' after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread on air is an idiom for being elated, so happy one seems to float.

clue.text: Language used by Giggs facing last of media

indicators.note: facing says the media letter stands in front of the footballer's name
last of points to the final letter of the word media

parts.note: Ryan Giggs is the Welsh footballer who played for Manchester United

explanation.surface: A footballer's choice of words when he faces the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryan Giggs is a famous Manchester United winger; 'facing' puts his first name after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aryan was an old name for the Indo-Iranian or Indo-European family of tongues.

clue.text: Not one Scottish adult visits Tyneside

indicators.note: visits says the adult letter goes into the regional abbreviation

parts.note: Tyneside, round Newcastle, lies in the North East of England, NE
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: No Scottish grown-up ever travels down to Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visits' places A inside NE. Tyneside is the area round Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means no or not, as in 'nae bother'.

clue.text: Stray bats sheltered inside colourful hollow rock

indicators.note: sheltered inside says the jumbled letters are tucked within the emptied word
hollow says the word colourful is emptied, leaving only its outer letters
bats, meaning crazy, says the letters of stray are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lost bats roost in a brightly coloured hollow rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but makes RYSTA from STRAY, and 'hollow' leaves C and L from colourful.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock crystal is clear quartz, a mineral that forms in geodes and rocky cavities.

clue.text: Whimsical and game bird briefly joins conservationists

indicators.note: briefly says the bird's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a quail is a small game bird
NT is the National Trust, the British conservation charity

explanation.surface: A quirky game bird teams up with a group of conservationists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' seems to go with 'Whimsical' but belongs to 'bird'. The NT is the National Trust, which preserves historic British buildings and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint means oddly old-fashioned or charmingly unusual, close to whimsical in sense.

clue.text: Before this time, some follow one refugee westbound

indicators.note: westbound in an across clue means the letters run right to left
some says only part of the run of words follow one refugee is used

explanation.surface: Some people trail after a refugee heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes WONERE from follow one refugee, and 'westbound' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic phrase meaning previously, up until the present moment.

clue.text: Rush from holiday forgetting time zones

indicators.note: forgetting says the holiday word loses the time letter

parts.note: Whit, or Whitsun, is a Christian festival and British holiday
Z is the abbreviation for zone, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone hurries home from a holiday, losing track of time zones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' drops T from WHIT, the Whitsun bank holiday in Britain, leaving WHI.
explanation.definitionFit: To whizz is to move very fast, so a hurried dash is a whizz.

clue.text: City hospital backed regulars involved in Nicky's birth

indicators.note: backed says the city and hospital letters are read in reverse

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a san, short for sanatorium, is a hospital

indicators.note: regulars involved in takes every other letter of the name, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A city hospital supports its regular visitors at the birth of Nicky's baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ECSAN into NASCE, and 'regulars' picks N, C, Y from Nicky.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascency is the state of coming into being, its origin or beginning.

clue.text: Mini car revolutionised transport

indicators.note: revolutionised, turned round, says the transport word is read in reverse

parts.note: trams are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A small car changed the way people travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mini' looks like the brand of car, but here it just says small.
explanation.definitionFit: The Smart is a tiny two-seater city car made by a Mercedes-Benz joint venture.

clue.text: Coach girl, showing golf film from 1990s

parts.note: a coach, the railway carriage sense, is a car
a lass is a girl
a film that is showing is on
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sports coach's daughter shows off her golf on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' reads as a trainer but is a railway carriage, CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1996 Ken Loach drama follows a Glasgow bus driver and a Nicaraguan refugee.

clue.text: One invents musical instrument we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a lyre is an ancient stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone creates a new musical instrument, or so we're told.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tells untruths invents stories, so the fabricator is a deceiver.

clue.text: Attaining job of clergyman when pastor leaves

indicators.note: leaves says the pastor letter departs from the clergyman's job

parts.note: preaching sermons is a clergyman's job

explanation.surface: A minister's career takes off once the pastor quits.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a goal or a place means arriving at it, achieving it.

clue.text: Type of ink I wanted when communicating

definitions.meaning: a dense black ink made from lampblack
the word radio operators use to spell out the letter I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer needed a certain ink to send a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a black drawing ink and the radio code word that stands for the letter I.

clue.text: Madness played loud tracks on campus

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the tracks after the campus letter

parts.note: F, for forte, is the musical direction for loud
a campus is a university, U
RY, for railway, means tracks

explanation.surface: The band Madness performed noisy songs at a university gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madness' reads as the 1980s ska band but is the definition; 'played' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is a wild rage, a frenzy close to madness.

clue.text: Overpower, with Ray, academic unknowns consumed by beer

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, an academic qualification

indicators.note: consumed by says the unknowns go down inside the beer

parts.note: ale is a beer
in algebra Z is an unknown, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A scholar named Ray drinks so much beer he is overcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a name but is part of the definition: a ray of light that blinds.
explanation.definitionFit: To dazzle is to overwhelm someone's sight with bright light, as a beam does.

clue.text: Section of cricket match's ending with belligerent men in charge

indicators.note: in says the letters go inside the charge word

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied

indicators.note: ending says take the final letter of the word match

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers of an army

explanation.surface: Part of a cricket match ends with aggressive players taking over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' seems to be the sport but is the insect, whose body has a middle section.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's body divides into head, middle section and abdomen; the middle one is this.

clue.text: Canoe at sea here?

indicators.note: at sea, meaning confused, says the letters of canoe are mixed up

explanation.surface: Asking where a small boat might be when it is out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges CANOE, and the whole clue points to where the canoe is.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe at sea is afloat on a vast body of salt water.

clue.text: Lay hands on chopped meat for this high-fibre bread?

indicators.note: chopped says the grabbing word loses its tail letter

parts.note: to lay hands on something is to grab it
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A request to snatch some sliced meat for a wholemeal sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' seems to go with the meat but cuts the last letter from GRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham flour is unsifted wholewheat flour, used for American wholemeal loaves and crackers.

clue.text: Wasps gathering made an attack, passing over street.

indicators.note: passing over says the street letters are skipped

parts.note: struck means attacked

explanation.surface: A swarm of insects attacks, missing the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Wasps is a rugby union club, so their gathering is a rugby scrum-like formation, not insects.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union a loose huddle of players over the ball on the ground is called by this name.

clue.text: Skirt's new, replaced by daughter for another type

indicators.note: replaced by says the new letter is swapped for the daughter letter

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A daughter swaps her brand-new skirt for a different style.
explanation.definitionFit: Midi is a skirt length reaching mid-calf, another style beside the mini and maxi.

clue.text: Haggard leader of squadron maintains a military aircraft?

indicators.note: maintains, holds, says the A sits inside the author's name and squadron letter

parts.note: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines

indicators.note: leader of points to the first letter of squadron

explanation.surface: A worn-out squadron commander keeps a warplane going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' seems to mean worn out but is the novelist H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiders are aircraft sent on bombing raids, warplanes attacking enemy targets.

clue.text: Pin-up said cool words half-exposed

indicators.note: half-exposed says only the back half of each of the two words is shown

explanation.surface: Someone said a few cool things while showing a little skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The back halves of SAID and COOL are ID and OL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a celebrity whose poster fans put up, someone adored and worshipped.

clue.text: Gents preserve big house?

definitions.meaning: a men's toilet, slang for the loo
to seal food in tins to keep it
the big house is US slang for prison, also called the slammer

explanation.surface: A query about whether a stately home keeps its men's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for both toilet and jail, and as a verb means to tin food.

clue.text: Removing monarchy last month leads to conflict around Norway

parts.note: Dec, December, is the last month of the year

indicators.note: around says the conflict word surrounds the Norway letter

parts.note: rowing means quarrelling, in conflict
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Last month, revolutionaries began abolishing kings after a war with Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a crown away from a ruler means deposing them, ending their reign.
